correctness.rationale: For finite positive bath temperature, gamma_+,gamma_->0 satisfying detailed balance and no added pure dephasing, Bloch evolution gives longitudinal p=e^-Gamma t and transverse sqrt(p). The coherent original has radius A(p) and population-inverted isospectral comparator radius B(p); Gibbs-relative entropy difference Delta(p)=(R-z)atanh(b)p-[S(B)-S(A)]. The exact squared radius gap is (R-z)(R+z+2b)p(1-p)>=0. Entropy derivative S(sqrt(q))=-h(q), h(q)=1/2 integral_0^1(1-qs^2)^-1 ds. Quadratic interpolation Q_theta between A^2 and B^2 satisfies Q+(1-p)Q_prime=R^2-a_theta(1-p)^2<=1. This makes the normalized gap Delta(p)/((R-z)p) strictly increase in p, even for pure initial vectors at every finite t. The normalized signs at p=1 and p->0 are positive and -((R+z)/(2b))atanh(b); coherence c>0 means -R<z<R, hence unique finite root. Cases c=0 are treated separately. Independent symbolic verification and direct numerical implicit root at b=.5,R=.8,z=0 gave p*=0.42993172972647203, t*=0.8441288509774865.

originality.rationale: Moroder et al. 2024 already construct an isospectral population-inverted Davies comparison and exhibit a sample free-energy crossing (Fig. 2 and Appendix A); that example and physical setup are prior. The inspected main paper and appendix do not prove strict global monotonicity of normalized difference for every coherent Bloch vector or uniqueness and if-and-only-if classification. Summer et al 2025 compare divergence-dependent crossover times in a wider resource-theoretic setup, not the same all-state theorem.
residual_risks: An exact all-initial-state monotone-crossing statement may appear in a later same-model paper not retrieved; searchable examples and generic resource-theory claims do not exhaust priority.
The strong conclusion does not extend to extra pure dephasing, driven/other Lindbladians or zero-temperature non-faithful Gibbs states.
